name: Username Generator - Build AD Wordlist from Names
description: Generates AD-style username permutations from a list of real names (first last). Produces common formats: first.last, flast, f.last, firstl, firstname, etc. Feed the output into kerbrute userenum to confirm valid usernames before spraying.
source: CPTS Module 13: Active Directory Enumeration & Attacks
notes:
=== WHY GENERATE USERNAMES ===
Password spraying requires a valid user list. Options:
  1. Extract via LDAP/RPC (requires domain access)
  2. Generate from names collected via OSINT (LinkedIn, company website, email headers)
  3. Enumerate via Kerberos pre-auth (kerbrute userenum — no credentials needed)

Username generation bridges OSINT → AD: you find names on LinkedIn, generate
possible AD usernames, validate them against Kerberos, then spray the valid set.

=== COMMON AD USERNAME FORMATS ===
  first.last        → john.smith         (most common in corporate)
  flast             → jsmith
  f.last            → j.smith
  firstlast         → johnsmith
  lastfirst         → smithjohn
  firstname         → john               (sometimes used in small orgs)
  FIRST.LAST        → JOHN.SMITH         (some orgs use uppercase)

Username-Anarchy generates all of these and more from a names file.

=== NAMES FILE FORMAT ===
Create a file with 'First Last' per line:
  John Smith
  Jane Doe
  Robert Brown
Sources: LinkedIn, company website (About Us), email signatures, OSINT tools.

=== VALIDATION STEP (CRITICAL) ===
Generated usernames include many invalid ones. Validate before spraying:
  kerbrute userenum -d inlanefreight.local --dc 172.16.5.5 generated_usernames.txt
Kerberos will confirm which accounts exist (KDC_ERR_C_PRINCIPAL_UNKNOWN = invalid).
This shrinks your spray target and avoids lockout attempts on non-existent accounts.

=== FULL CHAIN ===
1. Collect names via OSINT (LinkedIn, company site)
2. Username-Anarchy → generate_usernames.txt (this card)
3. kerbrute userenum → valid_users.txt (validate)
4. Check lockout policy (CME --pass-pol)
5. kerbrute passwordspray / CME / DomainPasswordSpray → valid creds
6. Evil-WinRM / BloodHound with valid creds

examples.label: Build names file from bash
examples.command:
cat << 'EOF' > names.txt
John Smith
Jane Doe
Robert Brown
EOF

defense.why_it_works: Generates likely AD username permutations (jsmith, john.smith, smithj...) from real employee names to feed spraying/enumeration.
defense.prerequisites: A list of employee names (from OSINT).
defense.impact: A username list for enumeration and spraying - offline generation, no target contact.
defense.detection: Offline/attacker-side generation - no target interaction at this step.
defense.prevention: [MITRE T1589.003] minimise public exposure of employee names/formats; the generated list only matters if downstream spraying succeeds - MFA + lockout defend that.
defense.misconfiguration: Active Directory usernames follow predictable naming conventions (firstname.lastname, f.lastname, firstnamelastname) that can be generated from publicly available employee data (LinkedIn, company website, email format leaks via OSINT). Without account lockout, generated username lists enable password spraying or AS-REP roasting enumeration.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Predictable username format discoverable via:
# Email signatures: john.smith@corp.com -> username = john.smith
# LinkedIn employee list + known naming convention = full user list
# OSINT: Hunter.io, phonebook.cz for email format detection

# No account lockout or username enumeration prevention:
# Kerbrute userenum runs 1000 names/second against DC Kerberos port
# Valid usernames confirmed without triggering any authentication failure log
defense.secure_config:
# 1. Adopt non-predictable username formats for privileged accounts:
# Use employee ID or random string for admin accounts
# Keep display names separate from login names

# 2. Lockout policy (applies to Kerberos username enumeration too):
Set-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy -LockoutThreshold 5 -LockoutDuration 00:30:00

# 3. Monitor Kerberos pre-auth failures (Event 4771):
# High volume of 4771 events from one source IP = username enumeration
# Microsoft Defender for Identity: 'Account enumeration reconnaissance' alert

# 4. Deploy honeypot accounts (valid username, never used legitimately):
# Any auth attempt for these accounts = attacker
# Immediate alert on Event 4625/4771 for honeypot usernames
defense.evasion: One password across many users, low-and-slow, staying under the lockout threshold and observed hours; validate a single hit before spraying wider.
